questions.question_text: You need to prevent the accidental deletion of a production virtual machine while still allowing updates to its configuration. Which type of Azure resource lock should you apply?
questions.explanation: According to Azure documentation, a CanNotDelete lock prevents deletion operations while allowing other updates.

questions.question_text: Which Azure management feature enables you to apply tags to a subscription so that they are automatically applied to resources created under that subscription?
questions.explanation: Azure Resource Manager (ARM) supports tagging at subscription scope, and tags propagate to resources created via ARM templates.

questions.question_text: You want to create an Azure Policy definition that blocks the creation of resources lacking a required 'Environment' tag. Which policy effect should you select?
questions.explanation: The Deny effect in Azure Policy prevents creation of resources that do not meet the compliance criteria, as described in the Azure Policy documentation.

questions.question_text: A company wants to ensure that all resources in a specific resource group have a 'CostCenter' tag and cannot be deleted. Which combination of Azure features should you use?

options.label: A
options.text: Azure Policy with audit effect and a ReadOnly lock

options.label: B
options.text: Azure Blueprint with tagging and a CanNotDelete lock

options.label: C
options.text: Azure Policy with deny effect and a CanNotDelete lock

options.label: D
options.text: Azure Advisor recommendations and Azure Monitor alerts

questions.explanation: Azure Policy with a Deny effect enforces the tag requirement, while a CanNotDelete lock stops deletion, matching the scenario described in Azure governance guidance.

questions.question_text: To set up a budget alert that emails the finance team when spending exceeds 80% of the budget, which Azure service provides the alert capability?
questions.explanation: Azure Cost Management (Budgets) lets you create alerts that trigger when spending reaches a defined percentage of the budget, per the Azure documentation.
